concept.name: Volume delta
concept.definition: The net difference between volume traded at the ask (aggressive market buys) and volume traded at the bid (aggressive market sells) over a price level, bar, or period. It measures which side initiated more traded volume, on the premise that market orders are what move prices. It is a descriptive order-flow statistic, not a predictive signal by itself.
concept.intuition: Delta answers 'who was more impatient — buyers or sellers?' Positive delta means buyers lifted more offers than sellers hit bids.
concept.mechanics: Every trade is classified as an ask trade (buy-initiated) or bid trade (sell-initiated); delta is then computed per footprint cell, per bar, or per period as ask-traded volume minus bid-traded volume, and displayed numerically or as a signed histogram.
concept.formula: Delta = V_ask − V_bid, where V_ask is volume traded at the ask (buyer-initiated) and V_bid is volume traded at the bid (seller-initiated)
concept.failure_modes: Trade-side classification degrades on feeds without exchange aggressor flags, and delta says nothing about passive limit-order flow — a large passive seller can absorb heavy positive delta while price still falls.
concept.misconceptions: Positive delta is not synonymous with rising price: bearish candles with positive delta are common when passive sellers absorb aggressive buying, so delta must be read against price response.
concept.example: A WTI crude trade of 25 contracts executes at the ask (delta +25) followed by 10 contracts at the bid (delta −10); net delta for the sequence is +15.
